ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Puncture-site precautions

A patient has just received systemic fibrinolytic therapy. A clinician considers an elective deep venous puncture at a site that cannot easily be compressed. Which concern best explains avoiding unnecessary invasive procedures during this period?

  1. Bleeding may be difficult to control at a noncompressible site
  2. The procedure always neutralizes the fibrinolytic
  3. Plasmin prevents all local anesthetic action
  4. Fibrinolysis causes immediate bacterial seeding
  5. The puncture converts venous blood into arterial blood
Answer and explanation

Bleeding may be difficult to control at a noncompressible site

Hemostasis is impaired, and inaccessible bleeding can be serious.

Option explanations

Bleeding may be difficult to control at a noncompressible site: Hemostasis is impaired, and inaccessible bleeding can be serious.

The procedure always neutralizes the fibrinolytic: A puncture does not chemically neutralize the drug.

Plasmin prevents all local anesthetic action: Local anesthetic activity is not universally prevented by plasmin.

Fibrinolysis causes immediate bacterial seeding: Bacterial seeding is not the direct fibrinolytic effect.

The puncture converts venous blood into arterial blood: Vessel puncture does not change blood identity.
